event_name: Jazz at The Strand: The Music of Dave Brubeck
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
If you've ever had Take Five on a playlist and quietly felt like you had good taste, this one's going to hit different.

The Jazz Legacy Project is bringing a full live performance of Dave Brubeck's iconic album Time Out to the Strand on Sunday afternoon. Time Out is one of the best-selling jazz albums ever recorded, and this isn't just a tribute band running through the tracks. The Jazz Legacy Project layers in storytelling alongside the music, walking the audience through the cultural context behind Brubeck's bold choices during the Civil Rights movement. It ends up feeling less like a concert and more like a really good documentary you can feel.

Founded in 2015, the Jazz Legacy Project has been selling out shows at the Velvet Note for six years straight. That kind of track record doesn't happen by accident. This is a Sunday afternoon well spent. Get your tickets before they go.
scoring_notes: High-income, highly educated adult audience with median age 38 is a strong fit for a curated jazz experience with cultural storytelling. The Jazz Legacy Project's consistent sellout history adds urgency. Sunday afternoon timing is ideal for the Perimeter mix of young professionals and empty nesters. Not a recurring weekly event — this is a specific one-night show.

venue: Springs Cinema & Taphouse, Sandy Springs, GA
blurb: Hadestown won eight Tony Awards in 2019, including Best Musical, and if you never caught it on Broadway or during its national tour, this is your shot at something close. Springs Cinema is screening the live theater capture of the original Broadway cast, which includes Reeve Carney and Eva Noblezada, at 4pm and 7pm on Friday. The show blends American folk music with New Orleans jazz to retell the myth of Orpheus and Eurydice, and it's genuinely unlike anything you've seen in a typical movie theater. You're sitting at the Taphouse with a drink in hand, watching a Tony-winning cast perform live on screen. Two shows to choose from, so you can actually plan dinner around it. This one's for the theater fans in East Cobb who've been meaning to see it.
scoring_notes: Educated, higher-income audience with a 42-year median age is squarely in the theater-appreciation demographic. Springs Cinema is close enough to East Cobb to be a reasonable outing.
